provenance.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE finished landscape 4:3 portrait for the Birdsong-to-Art collection. Final artwork for review, not a storyboard or a collage. These supplied pictures are artistic references only; do not borrow their species anatomy.
STYLE: sophisticated expressive ornithological illustration, slightly stylised through deliberate shape and line. Warm ivory cold-pressed paper, translucent watercolour underpainting, rich printed/gouache-like pigment with broken dry-grain edges, expressive dark ink contours, sharp directional coloured-pencil drawing. Organise plumage into clear pigment masses and rhythmic feather groups. Selected dark separations and pale feather edges articulate form; precise close-up work sits inside readable larger shapes. Retain the rich finish of the originals. Balance crisp face/selected feather passages with quieter areas, paper reserves and soft transitions. No blanket microtexture, equally heavy outline around everything, glossy digital shading, flat vector finish or giant cute eyes.
CHARACTER: the subject's genuine anatomy, a considered posture, long economical contours and fine feather rhythm create the charm. A small imaginative flourish in mark-making is welcome; avoid costumes, props, human expressions, leaf badges repeated from the originals and forced gags.
COMPOSITION: one dominant bird with its full silhouette comfortably inside the landscape canvas, subtle paper grain, generous quiet space and species-led colour. Background is simple abstract pigment geometry only, compatible with the bird's materials and palette. No scenery, foliage, nest, buildings, ornate frame or full habitat. A spare ink support is enough.
TEXT: only the exact species name specified below, understated dark handwritten lettering below the bird, as in the collection. No facts, jokes, subtitles, signature or watermark. Keep the lower-right corner quiet and empty: no activity or connectivity icon, no fabricated counts.
REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 is the PRIMARY original family style (Robin, Blackbird, Blue tit, Wren); image 2 supplies expressive contours and print texture; image 3 supplies fine drawn finish and restrained expression; image 4 calibrates clear feather grouping and selective structural contrast. None is an anatomical reference for the new bird.
SUBJECT: adult male Great Tit (Parus major). A clean glossy black crown and black throat, large WHITE CHEEKS, olive-green back, strong warm-yellow breast/belly with a broad BLACK CENTRAL STRIPE visibly running down its front, blue-grey wings and tail, a single white wingbar on each folded wing, small pointed black bill, natural slate-grey feet. Accurate Great Tit head pattern: no blue cap or Blue Tit eye-band. Dark eye with a small glint, no enlarged pale cartoon iris.
ARTISTIC INTENTION: alert and composed, a small sense of self-possession expressed by its bearing. Try a slightly turned frontal torso, face looking a little left, so the black breast stripe, white cheek and folded-wing bar all read. Give the body an elegant slightly angular poise, without stretching or inflating it. Species proportions stay true. Let cream/blue-grey feather edge drawing and varied black contours add individual rhythm; preserve the wingbar as a natural marking. It should feel authored like the first batch, not merely a realistic bird with a texture filter.
BACKGROUND DIRECTION: explore an economical offset angular pigment form in muted dusty lilac, related to the cool wings and contrasting the warm yellow; an exposed-paper interruption or asymmetrical crop may give a small surprise. Keep it subordinate and quite simple, distinct from the supplied circle/ochre arc/coral band. No background ornament.
TEXT verbatim: "Great tit".
